java_locations.role: Defines legacy key identity by lowercasing, removing underscore/dot separators, collapsing diagram-specific arrow prefixes, and rewriting a terminal `align` to `alignment`.
Reads `defaulttextalignment` through the canonical key lookup, so `default.text.align` is the same key.

rust_locations.role: Already ports Java key identity for reassignment collapse, but keeps the canonicalizer private and retains the latest normalized spelling in metadata.
Consumes retained metadata with direct case-insensitive string comparison, bypassing Java key identity and rejecting valid alias spellings at both value resolution and capability gates.

claimed_invariant: Every ordinary state skinparam lookup and state capability decision compares canonical Java key identities, not retained source spellings. Separator variants, diagram-specific arrow prefixes, and terminal align/alignment aliases therefore select the same value and rendering path.
causal_divergence: For `default.text.align`, Rust stores `defaulttextalign`. Its flat-label gate only admits `defaulttextalignment`, so the complete painted-envelope model is bypassed even though all actual painters are supported. The fallback leaves the Courier 11 UText top frontier unmeasured, producing the observed uniform 0.8032-pixel vertical displacement. Replacing only the fixture spelling with `default.text.alignment` makes the current implementation structurally equivalent, proving the geometry model itself is not the cause.
planned_model_change: Expose the parser's existing Java-derived canonical key function. Use it in shared state legacy-value resolvers, arrow-font lookup, SVEK spacing lookup, and autonomous/flat capability predicates. Preserve synthetic internal keys on paths that do not use ordinary skinparam identity. Add parser identity tests and a renderer regression using the original dotted/underscored alias spellings.
perturbation_axes: small Courier labels versus ordinary sans-serif labels
acceptance: The original dotted-key Courier counterexample is structurally equivalent without changing any metric or geometry constant.
Canonical and alias spellings produce the same parsed identity and no-oracle SVG.
Parser and renderer library suites pass.
An independent checker records a verdict at the exact implementation revision.
